chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever prefers forty of his brethren to himself and prays for them before he prays for himself, his prayer will be accepted for them and for himself.
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of praying for others before oneself in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this practice in *Al-Khisal* as a profound manifestation of *al-istijaba* (acceptance), where interceding for the community precedes personal petition. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity, suggesting that selfless advocacy for others amplifies the spiritual efficacy of one's own supplications.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-3 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn Abdul Jab’bar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of several of our companions that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
The prayers of whoever prefers forty of his brethren to himself and prays for them before he prays for himself would be accepted.”
